chapters.title: Start with one decision, not more data
A stopped machine in a hypothetical plant
Narrow commitments and choosing the first use case
Baselines, workflow walkthroughs and source readiness
Minimal cloud architecture, OT boundary and reliable ingestion
Storage choices, shared measures, data quality and access
Staffing, funding, testing, operation and scaling

takeaways: An industrial data platform should start from one recurring production decision with a named owner, such as which late orders need attention after a machine stops, not from connecting every machine and system.

Before building, measure the current checking and waiting time, walk through real incidents, test source records with an actual order and agree on shared definitions for machines, resources, operations and quantities.

A minimal architecture of supported connectors, Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, with Azure only where a gap requires it, keeps production control local and lets the team scale by gates based on demonstrated evidence.
hook: Many mid-sized manufacturers have ERP, MES and machine data, yet planners still cannot tell which production decision needs to change before the next shift. This episode is for CIOs, IT and OT managers and data leaders in mid-sized manufacturing who need a data platform roadmap their small team can actually run. You will learn how to pick a first use case, prove value with a baseline, keep the architecture minimal and expand step by step without letting the platform outgrow the team.
